This Statute shall be inconsistent as applicable with the Animal Act, No. 29 of 1958 as amendedby the Act, No. 10 of 1968, the Act, No. 46 of 1988 and the Act, No. 10 of 2009; the Animal Feed Act,No. 10 of 1986; the Butchers Ordinance No. 9 of 1893; the Animal Diseases Act, No 59 of 1992; theEpidemic Act, No. 33 of 1952; Anti Rabies Act, No. 23 of 1956; Veterinary Surgeons and PractitionersAct, No. 16 of 1998; Butches Act, of 1968; and the Meat Inspection Act, of 2004.
Be it enacted by the Provincial Council of North Western Province of the Democratic Social-ist Republic of Sri Lanka as follows :
01. This Statute may be cited as the Livestock Statute No. ……. of 2016 of the Provincial
Council of the North Western Province.
02. This Statute shall come into operation on such date as may be appointed by the Governor of
the North Western Province.
03. Objectives of the Statute:
(1) To provide for the planning, formulation, implementation, operation and regulation of
policies relating to livestock in compliance with the national policies and needs of theprovince;
(2) To provide for the preservation, regulation, caring, improving of livestock and production
and use of animal feed and medicines and prevention of animal diseases;
(3) To establish the North Western Provincial Department of Animal Productions and Health;
(4) To establish the North Western Provincial Livestock Development Committee;
Livestock Statute No. …………….. 0f 2016 of the Provincial Council of the North
Western Province

A statute to provide for the implementation of Provincial Livestock Policies towards a SustainableDevelopment in the North Western Province; for the realization of objectives; for the formulation,implementation and operation of plans with regard to the preservation, taking care and development oflivestock and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto and to provide for the repeal ofNorth Western Provincial Animal Husbandry Statute No.04 of 1998.

(5) To empower famers engaged in the livestock sector in the North Western Province;
(6) To establish Zonal and Regional Livestock Development Committees and Rural Livestock
Development Societies of those engaged in the livestock sector in the North WesternProvince;
(7) To ensure the maintenance of environment friendly farms of prescribed standard and
healthy and qualitative animal production in the province;
(8) To establish and maintain the North Western Provincial Diary Promotion Fund.
PART I
Policy Planning, Management and Regulation
04. The Provincial Ministry in charge of the subject shall be vested with the policy planning on

animal production and development in the North Western Province in compliance with thenational policy and needs of the province for which purpose, proposals from the Rural, Regional,Zonal and Provincial Livestock Committees established within the province may be sought.
05. The Provincial Director shall prepare a five year Provincial Livestock Development Plan
giving due consideration to the proposals referred to at Section 04 above and submit same forthe approval of the Provincial Livestock Development Committee once in every five years.
06. The Provincial Ministry and the Department in charge of the subject shall provide livestock
and health, breeding, extension, training, marketing, promotion and provincial research servicesneeded by those engaged in livestock sector within the province.
07. The Animal Development Advisory Divisions, Regional Veterinary Medical Officer’s Divisions
and Zones shall be demarcated on the basis of the National policy and extension of thepopulation, extent of land, animal population, climatic conditions and administrative boundariesin the province.
08. Research Institutions may be established and maintained for the needs of the province.
09. Human resources development Divisions or Units may be established for the purpose of
empowering stakeholders with a view to promoting livestock development.
PART II
Establishment, composition, powers and functions of the Provincial Department of Animal
Production and Health
10. There shall be established a Department which shall be called “North Western Provincial
Department of Animal Production and Health” (herein after referred to as the “Department”)to implement the provisions and to achieve objectives of this Statute.

11. The North Western Provincial Department of Animal Production and Health shall, by the
name assigned to it be a body corporate and shall have a perpetual succession and a commonseal and may carry out all functions related to the livestock sector and sue and be sued in suchname.
12. The Governor of the North Western Province shall with the concurrence of the Provincial

Minister in-charge of the subject, appoint a Class I Veterinary Medical Officer of the AnimalProduction and Health Service to the post of North Western Provincial Director of AnimalProduction and Health (hereinafter referred to as the “Director”) to exercise the powers vestedin the Department.
13. For the purpose of execution of the duties and functions of the Department there may be
appointed Additional Provincial Directors, Subject Specialists, Deputy Directors, VeterinaryMedical officers, Animal Husbandry Officers, Animal Development Instructors, and otherancillary staff.
14. All officers and employees who are in service of the North Western Provincial Department
of Animal Production and Health on the day of coming into operation of this Statute shall bedeemed to have appointed under this Statute.
15.(1) Powers to execute the directions and orders made for the purpose of provisions of this
Statue and matters incidental thereto shall be vested in the Director subject to the generaladministration of the Secretary.
(2) The Director may exercise the powers vested in him by delegating such powers to other
officers of the Department as the case may be.
(3) The Director shall account to the Secretary for the management of all physical, financial
and human resources including moveable and immoveable assets of the Department.
16.(1) The Provincial Director or any other officer duly authorized by the Director shall have
the powers to enter and inspect any farm or manufacturing plant or sales centre or coldstorage at any time for the purpose of execution of provisions of this Statute.
(2) No person shall obstruct any authorized officer exercising his powers under this Statute
or regulations made there under.
(3) The owner or the person in charge of or every person present at the site subjected to
inspection shall be bound to provide the officer carrying out the inspection undersubsection (1) above with samples or other information as required by the officer incarrying out his duties.
(4) No person shall provide false or misleading samples or information to any officer engaged
in obtaining samples or information in a formal manner.
17. The Department shall execute following functions for the development, preservation, extension
and regularization of livestock in the province:
(1) to formulate and implement the annual plan in compliance with five year Plan;
(2) to ensure healthcare of animal by control, prevention of and treatment to animal disease;

(3) to carry out breeding for the maintenance of an environmental friendly animal population
of high genetic quality which suits the needs of the province;
(4) to implement extension and training programmes;
(5) to implement production and sales promotional programmes;
(6) to conduct provincial researches and surveys and publicize their results;
(7) to introduce new technology and farm mechanizations which suit the province;
(8) to liaise with research institutes of national, provincial and regional level, universities
and other institutes related to animal husbandry;
(9) to introduce and sale high quality breeding and plant materials necessary for the
development of animal farming;
(10) to register, issue licenses to, supervise and regulate rural, regional, zonal livestock

development committees, animal farms, animal caretakers, distributors, mobile sellers,producers and distributors of veterinary medicines, equipment and feed and all voluntaryorganizations and individuals involved in the livestock sector;
(11) to maintain and update all data bases related to livestock sector;
(12) to ensure hygiene and quality of animal productions and standardization of farms;
(13) to maintain laboratories to commensurate with the needs of the province;
(14) to prevent and control animal diseases in the province;
(15) to provide for and regulate the environmental friendly animal farms, processing plants,
cold storages, sales outlets, in accordance with accepted standards;
(16) to prevent and control diseases transmitted from animals to humans;
(17) to ensure animal welfare;
(18) to grant permission to transport animal within North Western Province;
(19) to organize provincial exhibitions and competitions in relation to the livestock sector
in order to appreciate those who are engaged in the sector;
(20) to inspect accounts of and give necessary advice to rural, regional and zonal livestock
development committees;
(21) to regulate manufacture, sale, and use of animal feed, animal breeding matters, veterinary
medicines, and chemicals.
18.(1) The Annual Development Plan for the ensuing year pertaining to the development of

the Livestock Institutions and Promotion of Animal Husbandry based on the ProvincialLivestock Development Plan prepared in keeping with the provisions of the Section 05of this Statue should be submitted by the Director to the Secretary for approval prior to31st of October.

PART III
Registration of Institutions and individuals
19. Every farm, manufacturing plant, sales outlets, cold storage, rural, regional or zonal livestock

development committee related to livestock sector in the North Western Province, everyanimal caretaker, distributor, mobile salesman, producer or distributor of veterinary medicines,equipment or animal feed, every institute, voluntary organization or individual that purchaselivestock produced in the North Western Province shall obtain and annually renew theCertificate of Registration issued by the Director.
20. For the purpose of registration, the applicant shall:
(1) make the application on the specimen prescribed by the Director;
(2) pay a registration fee as prescribed by the Minister;
(3) comply with the criteria and standards specified by regulations made under Section 84
(1) of this Statute;
(4) fulfill all other legal requirements as required.
21. No person shall transfer or alienate the certificate of registration or alter any information
contained therein without the approval of the Director.
22. The Director shall not entertain any application for registration made under Section 19 unless
it meets the requirements specified in Section 20 and shall inform thereof to the applicant inwriting.
23.(1) When the Director determines that any institution, individual or volunteer organization

that has been registered under Section 19 of this Statute, acts in contravention of theobjectives of the Statute or does not comply with the standards specified by regulations,the registration of such institution, individual or volunteer organization may betemporarily suspended.
(2) In the event of temporarily suspension of registration, the Director shall inform in writing
the reasons lead to such suspension to the holder of the Certificate of Registration.
(3) When the registration is temporarily suspended, if the institution, individual or volunteer

organization whose registration is so suspended takes actions to make good the reasonslead to such suspension and to meet the stipulated requirements within a reasonabletime as determined by the Director, the registration of such institution, individual orvolunteer organization shall be reinstated.
24. If the institution, individual or volunteer organization whose registration has been suspended

fails to meet the requirements within the stipulated reasonable time as per Section 23 (3) ofthis Statute, the Director shall cancel the registration and inform thereof to the institution,individual or volunteer organization concerned.

25. The party which is in receipt of a notice to the effect that the application for the registration

was rejected under Section 22 of this Statute or that the registration was cancelled underSection 24, may make an appeal there from to the Minister in charge of the subject within 45days from the receipt of such notice.
26.(1) When an appeal is received under Section 25 of this Statute the Minister shall direct the
Secretary to conduct an inquiry and determine thereon.
(2) The Secretary after conducting an inquiry shall make recommendations to the Minister
to confirm or revise or reject the determination of the Director.
(3) The Secretary shall submit his recommendations within 45 days from the receipt of the
appeal and the decision of the Minister thereon shall be final and conclusive.
27.(1) When a person who has been convicted of the offence of maintaining a farm, cold storage,

manufacturing plant or sales outlet without a license issued under this Statute orregulations made thereunder, continues to maintain the farm, cold storage, manufacturingplant or sales outlet, an order may be issued on a request made in that regard by theDirector or any other person authorized by him, directing such person to close downsuch farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet until such time the personconcerned obtains a license again.
(2) In any proceeding under subsection (1) above, the certificate issued by the Director or

any other officer duly authorized by him shall be prima facie evidence of the contenttherein to the effect that the person whose name appears on the certificate continues tomaintain the farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or the sales outlet without a license.
(3) Provided however that, in the event of submission of an appeal under Section 25 of this
Statute, the closure shall be deferred pending the determination of the appellate inquiry.
(4) When the decision of the Director is confirmed at the appellate inquiry and under Section
23 (2) of this Statute, action shall be taken to close down within 30 days from the dateof the appellate determination.
28. When the Director identifies any premises as a threat to the maintenance of animal welfare of
the province, he shall obtain a temporary closing order in that regard from a Magistrate court.
29.(1) When any person fails to comply with the closing order issued under Section 27(1) of

this Statute, the Magistrate shall issue an order requiring and authorizing the fiscal ofthe court to close down the farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outletmentioned in the said order and the fiscal shall execute such order on a date prior to notlater than seven full days or sooner than three full days from the date of the order. Theorder shall be sufficient authority for the fiscal or any other police officer authorizedby him for the purpose to enter the farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or salesoutlet together with the assistants deemed necessary for the purpose of closing downsuch farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet.

PART IV
Provincial Livestock Development Committee
30. There shall be established a Provincial Livestock Development Committee to facilitate the

implementation of the Livestock Statute of the Province. The Provincial Minister in chargeof the subject of Livestock shall be the Chairman of the Committee and the Secretary to theProvincial Ministry in charge of the subject of Livestock shall be the Secretary to theCommittee. This Committee may function in collaboration with the Provincial AgricultureCommittee and Provincial Irrigation Committee.
31.(1) The constitution of the Committee shall be as follows:
I. five Council Members nominated by the Advisory Committee to the Provincial Ministry
in charge of the subject of Livestock to represent each Veterinary Medical Officer’sDivision;
II. District Secretaries of the Districts of Kurunegala and Puttlam or their representatives;
III. North Western Provincial Director of Animal Production and Health;
IV. North Western Provincial Director of Agriculture;
V. North Western Provincial Director of Irrigation;
VI. Deputy and Assistant Commissioners of Agrarian Services of the Districts of Kurunegala
and Putlam;
VII. North Western Provincial Commissioners of Land:
VIII. North Western Provincial Director of Health;
IX. North Western Provincial Commissioners of Co-operative Development;
X. Director of North Western Provincial Environment Authority;
XI. a representative nominated by the Director General of the Department of Animal
Production and Health;
XII. District Managers of the Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board;
XIII. Deputy Directors in charge of zones of the Provincial Department of Animal Production
and Health;
XIV. Representatives of State banks as determined;
XV. Chairpersons of Zonal Livestock Development Committees;
XVI. A Provincial Representative of the Livestock Development Board;
XVII. Three Heads of Institutes involved in livestock Development;
XVIII. Three representatives of Dairy Purchasing Institutions on order of purchase.

(2) The Committee may co-opt the representatives or individuals of organizations and
institutions for the deliberations of the Committee as may be determined by the Minister.
32. The members mentioned under I to XIII in subsection 31 (1) of this Statute shall be ex-officio
members of the Committee and those other members mentioned under XIV to XVI may beappointed by the Minister at his discretion.
33. The term of office of the members appointed by the Minister shall be two years.
34. Where a member appointed by the Minister vacates office by expiry of term of office,
resignation, removal by the Minister at his discretion, absence from three consecutive meetingsor death or insanity, the Minister shall fill the vacancy so created.
35. The Provincial Committee shall meet at least once in every two months and if found necessary
the Secretary may convene supplementary meetings of the Committee on the direction of theChairman.
36. (1). The quorum of the Committee shall be ¼ of the membership.
(2). The existence of vacancies in the Committee shall not hinder the conduct of meetings
of the Committee or the making of decisions at such meetings.
37. The functions of the Provincial Livestock Development Committee shall be:-
(1) to submit recommendations and proposals for the formulation of policies pertaining to
matters stipulated in this Statute in compliance with the National Policy and needs ofthe province;
(2) to provide necessary advice for the operation and implementation of matters stipulated
in the Statute;
(3) to approve the five year Livestock Development Plan and other long term and medium
term development plans forwarded to the Committee;
(4) to take follow up actions and to review the formulation and implementation of the
Provincial Livestock Development Policy while providing necessary resources,guidance and assistance for the same;
(5) to grant prior approval for any programme or project for the extension and promotion

of and education on livestock, provision of services and for researches on livestock tobe implemented within the province by any governmental or non-governmentalorganization, institution, foundation, society, project, programme or similar institution,individual or group of persons and to take appropriate action when relevant conditionsare violated.
38.(1) The Committee may make procedures for the conduct of business of the meetings of
the Committee.
(2) The members of the Committee participating in the meetings thereof may be remunerated
at such rates as may be determined by the Minister and be approved by the Governor.

PART V
Rural Livestock Development Societies
39. The farmers engaged in livestock activities in a Grama Niladhari Division or any part thereof

or several divisions may get together and set up Rural Livestock Development Societies foreach field of Animal Husbandry or amalgamating two or more such fields and every suchsociety shall be registered with the Department.
40. Rural Livestock Development Society shall, by the name assigned to it be a body corporate
and shall have perpetual succession and a common seal and may carry out all functions relatedto the livestock sector and may sue and be sued in such name.
41. The object of setting up of these societies shall be to develop the livestock sector by mobilizing
those who are engaged in the livestock sector at rural level and thereby empowering them.The object of setting up of societies
42. Qualifications to be eligible for membership:
(1) to be a citizen of Sri Lanka;
(2) to be not less than 18 years of age;
(3) the farm to be located within the area of authority of the Livestock Development Society;
(4) the farm to have registered with the Department of Animal Productions.
43. Every Rural Livestock Development Society shall appoint an executive committee comprising
of Chairman, Secretary, Treasure, Vice-chairman, Co-Secretary, and six members and the termof office of such office bearers shall be one year from the appointment.
44. (1) The Director shall prepare the constitution for the Rural Livestock Development
Societies which shall be approved by the Minister.
(2) Every Rural Livestock Development Society shall comply with the constitution.
45. The powers and functions of Rural Livestock Development Societies:
(1) to formulate and implement livestock development plan for the area of authority of the
society in compliance with the provincial plan and coordinate and regulate theimplementation of the said plan;
(2) to facilitate and liaise with relevant institutions for the development of farms of members;
(3) to resolve issues relating to livestock sector arising within the area of authority of the
society;
(4) to maintain an updated data base relevant to the sector and disseminate such data to
relevant parties when the need arises;
(5) to implement loan schemes for members of the society;
(6) to implement programmes to enhance the funds of the society;

46.(1) The Secretary shall convene meetings of the Society once in every month or two months
and may convene supplementary meetings of the Society at the request of the majorityof members.
(2) The quorum of the meetings shall be more than 1/3 of the membership.
47.(1) When a member vacates office by reason of :
I. resignation;
II. absence from three consecutive meetings;
III. death or insanity;
IV. removal at the will of the majority members on grounds of any breach of the
Statute or distancing from the livestock sector; such member shall cease to be amember.
(2) When a member ceases to be a member or resigns or is removed at the will of the
majority members, the office of such member shall cease.
48. There shall be paid into the Rural Livestock Development Fund:
I. the membership subscription;
II. donations by the State, Provincial, Non-governmental organizations;
III. donations by individuals;
IV. interest and dividends of the fund;
V. All money received from other sources.
49. The Account of the Fund.
(1) The account of the Fund shall be maintained in a State Bank and the accounts of fund shall be
maintained as provided by the constitution of the society.
(2) The Director or any other officer authorized by him shall examine the accounts of the Fund
annually or as appropriate.
50.(1) The supervision of the affairs of, examination of books of and providing guidance and
advice to Rural Livestock Development Societies established within his area of authorityshall be vested in the Animal Development Advisor.
(2) Any officer duly authorized by the director for the purpose may supervise and examine
the books of Rural Livestock Development Societies.

51. (1). The Director shall appoint a staff grade public officer as the liquidator to cancel the
registration and to liquidate any registered Rural Livestock Development Society onany one or more of the following grounds:
(i) the membership declines to less than eleven;
(ii) being defunct for a period exceeding one year;
(iii) has acted contrary to its objects;
(iv) number of members not less than two thirds (2/3) of the membership making a
request to the Director citing that the society has failed to act for the achievementof its objectives.
(2). The liquidator appointed under Subsection 51(1) above shall have the following powers
subject to the prior approval of the Secretary to the provincial Ministry in charge of thesubject:
(i) to determine the priority among the creditors of the society;
(ii) to sale properties of the society;
(iii) to settle any claims by or against the society;
(iv) to distribute assets of the society as required.
(3). The Liquidation Notice of the liquidator shall be published in newspapers published in
all three languages viz Sinhala, Tamil and English.
(4). When a society is liquidated, the fund of the society shall be used for the settlement of
liquidation expenses in the first instance and thereafter for the settlement of its liabilities.The surplus of funds on liquidation shall be credited to the Dairy Promotion Fund.
PART VI
Regional Livestock Development Committee
52. There shall be established a Regional Livestock Development Committee for each Regional
Veterinary Medical Officer’s Division and be registered with the Department.
53.(1) The Director shall prepare the Constitution of the Regional Livestock Development
Committees which shall be approved by the Minister.
(2) Every Regional Livestock Development Committee shall act in compliance to the said
constitution.
54. (1). The Committee shall constitute of the followings;
(i) Veterinary Medical Officer;
(ii) Animal Development Instructors;

(iii) Ten members elected by the majority vote of the representatives nominated by
Rural Livestock Development Societies;
(iv) An Agro Development Officer;
(v) A Public Health Inspector;
(vi) An Agriculture Instructor nominated by the Provincial Director of Agriculture;
(vii) A Coconut Development Officer;
(viii) An officer involved in the sector nominated by the Divisional Secretary ;
(ix) An Environmental Officer of a Local Authority;
(x) Regional Agents of Dairy Purchasing Companies within the North Western Province.
(2). Where a nominated member vacates office, the Deputy Director in charge of the Zones
shall on the recommendation of the Veterinary Medical Officer, nominate anothermember to represent the relevant field of the member who vacates office.
55. The representatives of governmental, non-governmental and private organizations engaged in

the livestock sector may obtain the associated membership of the Committee with the approvalof the Committee and they shall not be entitled to voting at the meetings or to hold any officeof the Committee.
56. The Chairperson of the Regional Livestock Development Committee shall be elected from
among the members of Rural Livestock Development Societies and the Veterinary MedicalOfficer of the Division shall be the ex-officio Secretary to the Committee.
57. The term of office of the non ex-officio members shall terminate when they cease to be
members of the society they represent.
58. Meetings of the Committee shall be convened once in every three months and the quorum of
such meeting shall be over 1/3 of the membership.
59. Functions of the Committee shall be as follows:
(1) to formulate the Regional Livestock Development Plan based on the Provincial
Livestock Development Plan;
(2) to formulate special project proposals in accordance with the regional potentialities
and to seek financial provisions for the same while coordinating among other relevantinstitutions;
(3) to provide necessary assistance and guidance to formulate the Rural Livestock
Development Plan;
(4) to take action on matters referred to the Committee by the Rural Livestock Development
Societies;
(5) to ensure the efficient and effective utilization of funds received for the livestock sector;
(6) To nominate representatives to the Zonal Livestock Development Committee;

PART VII
Zonal Livestock Development Committee
60. There shall be established a Zonal Livestock Development Committee for each zone as
demarcated under Section 7 of this Statute and shall be registered with the Department.
61. The Director shall prepare the constitution of the Zonal Livestock Development Committees
which shall be approved by the Minister and every Zonal Livestock Development Committeeshall act in compliance to the said constitution.
62. The constitution of the Committee shall be as follows:
(1) Deputy Director in-charge of the Zone;
(2) Chairpersons of Regional Livestock Development Committees;
(3) four Veterinary Medical Officers appointed by the Director;
(4) four senior Animal Development Instructors appointed by the Director;
(5) a Livestock Investigation Officer;
(6) an Assistant Director Nominated by the Director;
(7) representatives of the Livestock Development Board and dairy purchasing companies;
(8) a representative of the Agrarian Insurance Board ;
(9) a representative of the District Secretary;
(10) a representative of the Central Environment Authority;
(11) District Health Services Director or his representative.
63. The representatives of governmental, non-governmental and private organizations engaged in

the livestock sector may obtain the associated membership of the Committee with the approvalof the Committee and they shall not be entitled to voting at the meetings or to hold any officeof the Committee.
64. The Chairperson of the Zonal Livestock Development Committee shall be elected from among
the Chairpersons of Regional Livestock Development Committees and the Deputy Directorin charge of the Zone shall be the ex-officio Secretary to the Committee.

PART VIII
Diary Development Fund
68. There shall be established a Fund hereinafter referred to as the Dairy Development Fund.
69. The Fund by the name assigned to it be a body corporate and shall have perpetual succession
and a common seal and may carry out all functions related to the livestock sector and may sueand be sued in such name.
70. The Director of the North Western Provincial Department of Animal Production and Health
shall be responsible for the administration of the Fund.
71. There shall be appointed a Board of Management for the administration, management and
control of the Dairy Development Fund.
72.(1) The Board of Management of the Dairy Development Fund hereinafter referred to as
the “Fund” shall constitute of the following:
(I) Secretary to the Provincial Ministry in-charge of the subject;
(II) the Regional manager of the MILCO Ltd. and two agents of two dairy purchasing
private companies;
(III) a specialist in the field of dairy farming;
(IV) three representatives engaged in the dairy sector and nominated by the Zonal
Livestock Development Committees.

PART IX
General
84.(1) The Minister shall issue necessary instructions, guidance and orders for the
implementation of provisions of the Statute.
(2) The Minister shall demarcate the divisions referred to in Section 7 of this Statute and
such demarcations shall be published in the Gazette.
(3) The Minister shall have the power to impose restrictions as appropriate in transporting
animals within and out of the province.
(4) The Minister shall have the power to make regulations in respect of prevention and
control of animal diseases within the province.
85.(1) Every regulation made by the Minister under Section 84 (1) of this Statute shall be
published in the Gazette and shall come into operation on the date of such publicationor on such date as may be specified in such regulation.
(2) Every regulation made by the Minister shall as soon as it is convenient after its publication

in the Gazette, be brought before the Provincial Council for approval. Any regulationwhich is not so approved by the Provincial Council shall be deemed to be rescinded asfrom the date of disapproval but without prejudices to anything previously madethereunder and a notification of the date on which any such regulation is deemed rescindedshall be published in the Gazette.
86.(1) Any person aggrieved by any regulation made under this Statute or by any order or decision
made by any officer, may prefer an appeal to the Minister.
(2) The Minister may affirm, vary or amend the order or decision against which the appeal
has been preferred on the recommendation made by an officer or a Board of Inquiryappointed by the Secretary by order of the Minister, after an inquiry into the matter.
87. Every party registered under Section 19 shall provide accurate information relating to the
livestock sector on demand to the Director.
88. Every institute which is registered under Section 19 and engaged in purchasing milk, meat and

eggs produced in the province, shall submit to the Director a monthly report indicating theamounts it purchased during the month in the format as may be specified by the Directorbefore the 15th day of the following month.
89. Every institute which is registered under Section 19 of this Statute and purchases more than
1000 liters of milk a day shall make a contribution of Rupees one for every liter of milk itpurchases to the Dairy Development Fund.

PART X
Offences and Penalties
91. Every person who contravenes any provisions of this Statute or any regulation made thereunder
shall be guilty of an offence under this Statute.
92 Every person who contravenes or fails to comply with any provision of Sections 16, 19, 21,

87, 88, 89 and 90 of this Statute or any regulation made thereunder shall on conviction aftersummary trial by a Magistrate be punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12months or to a fine not exceeding rupees hundred thousand or to both such fine andimprisonment.
93. Where an offence under this Statute is committed, the Provincial Director or any other officer
authorized by him shall have the power to institute action.
